newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: MOTOR RACING-BERGER TO QUIT BENETTON AT END OF YEAR.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BERGER TO QUIT BENETTON AT END OF YEAR.

text.p: Formula One driver Gerhard Berger said on Thursday he would not drive for the Benetton team next season, the Austrian news agency APA reported.

"One thing is certain, I will definitely not be with Benetton next year," said Berger, who is returning to the circuit at the German Grand Prix this weekend after missing the last three races of the world championship because of a recurring sinus infection.

The 37-year-old Austrian told a news conference in Hockenheim he did not know which team he would join or if he would quit Formula One altogether. He said he would make a decision about his future in the next two to three weeks.
"I have a few options, also some outside of motor racing. I will remain in Formula One only if I can drive for a top team," he said. He denied reports he was holding talks with other teams.
Berger said he had been unable to make a decision due to his six-week illness and the death of his father. Johann Berger was killed when his private jet crashed in Austria two weeks ago.
"It is a bad idea to make a decision when times are difficult," said Berger, the oldest driver on the circuit who has contested 202 races and won nine.
Benetton said on Tuesday they had signed Italian Giancarlo Fisichella for next year.

APA said Benetton's French driver Jean Alesi could be replaced next season by Austrian Alexander Wurz, who deputised for Berger in the last three races and finished a surprise third at the British Grand Prix at Silverstone.
Berger and Alesi have failed to win a race since joining Benetton at the start of last season.
